newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Toyota inaugurates plant in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Toyota inaugurates plant in Argentina.

text.p: Toyota Motor Co will open Friday a $150 million plant in Argentina to make Hilux pickups for sale both in the domestic market and in the country's partners in the customs union Mercosur.
The company plans to make this year 10,000 units of the 4x4 and 4x2 single- and double-cabin Hiluxes in the new plant in Zarate, 50 miles (80 km) north of Buenos Aires.
Production is scheduled to double next year.
Half of the vehicles will be sold to Argentina's partners in Mercosur -- Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.

In December the company laid the foundation stone in the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo of another plant where it will make its flagship Corolla from 1998. More than 20 million Corollas have been sold since 1969.

The firm aims to capture a 10 percent share of the Mercosur auto market by 2000 with estimated sales of 300,000 vehicles in South America. It also has plants in Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela. Its South American plants produced a total of 27,897 vehicles last year.
Toyota employs 70,000 people in 26 countries and last year its revenues were $190 billion.
